problem:
$$
f(t,y)=⟨\text{_____},\,y,\,2\operatorname{sec}⁡t⟩,\,t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})
$$

The vector-valued function $f(t,y)$ above parametrizes one sheet of the hyperbolic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as ${z}^{2}-{x}^{2}=4$ for $z\ge 2.$ What is the first component of $f?$

feedback.problem:
$$
f(x,t)=⟨x,\,\text{_____},\,7\operatorname{tan}⁡t⟩,\,t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})
$$

The vector-valued function $f(x,t)$ above parametrizes one sheet of the hyperbolic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as ${y}^{2}-{z}^{2}=49$ for $y\ge 7.$ What is the second component of $f?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that the hyperbola ${y}^{2}-{z}^{2}=49$ for $y\ge 7$ in $yz$-plane has the parametrization

$$
⟨y,z⟩=⟨7\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,7\operatorname{tan}⁡t⟩,\,t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})
$$

since 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}-{z}^{2} & =(7\operatorname{sec}⁡t)^{2}-(7\operatorname{tan}⁡t)^{2} \\  & =49{sec}^{2}⁡t-49{tan}^{2}⁡t \\  & =49({sec}^{2}⁡t-{tan}^{2}⁡t) \\  & =49.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,t) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨x,\,7\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,7\operatorname{tan}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})$ and $x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Therefore, the second component of $f$ is $7\operatorname{sec}⁡t.$
